subject: Performance SLO (p95/p99) qualification - Hosted API vs current provider - post-call recap

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Performance SLO (p95/p99) qualification - Hosted API vs current provider - post-call recap

Hi Alex / Samir,

Thanks again for spending time today — good conversation. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment on the performance targets you called out and how Redwood would approach validation.

Recap (what you shared on the call):
- Target end-to-end p95: ~200ms (short prompts / chat-turns)
- Target end-to-end p99: <=450ms (for 90% of flows; some large-context tails acceptable)
- Throughput: baseline ~150-250 QPS for the inference endpoint, burst to 400 QPS
- Concurrency: ~40-60 concurrent active streams
- Streaming: partial-token streaming for interactive chat is required (low token-latency on first partial token)
- Current provider: you reported p95 ~480ms, p99 ~1.1s in production traces (with occasional >2s tails during load spikes)

What Redwood proposes / measures:
- We measure end-to-end at the API ingress to final token emitted (includes our network + runtime latency; excludes customer client-side network).
- For streaming, we report both time-to-first-byte (TTFB) for first partial token and time-per-additional-token when streaming enabled.
- To hit p99 targets at your concurrency, we recommend testing in "dedicated" or reserved capacity profile during evaluation (avoids noisy neighbor effects).

Attachments / links:
- Attached: redwood-p95-p99-sla-table.xlsx (SLA table & measurement definitions)
- Attached: perf-sample-results.pdf (example sample-run from a customer with similar footprint)
- Shared drive: https://drive.google.com/finlytics/redwood-perf-plan (detailed eval plan)

Proposed next steps:
1) Share a short sample workload (5-10 representative prompts + token distribution) and a short runbook for how you make requests today (headers, streaming usage).
2) Redwood provides a one-week hosted eval with a reserved capacity profile. We will run distributed load tests and a production-like streaming run.
3) Schedule a 30-min tech-run where our infra lead (Jonas) walks through test harness, credentials, and test vectors.
4) After the evaluation we deliver a p95/p99 report with configuration recommendations (batching/quantization/routing).

Are you available for a tech-run Thurs or Fri this week?

Thanks,

Laura Bennett
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Thanks Laura — appreciate the clear summary.

A few clarifying points from our side after reviewing the notes:
- The current provider numbers I quoted were from our edge metrics (client-side + provider network); I attached a short trace (finlytics-trace-0415.log) that shows where we see the tails stack up.
- Region: we need the eval to run from us-west and eu-west regions — can you replicate both?
- Cold-start behavior: for short-lived models we see spikes when a new worker spins up. How does Redwood measure/mitigate cold starts in hosted mode?
- Streaming: our main complaint is time-to-first-token consistency under load — any initial guidance on guarantees or how you report that would help us frame success.

We can do a tech-run Friday morning PST. Also interested in any documentation that spells out exactly what you include for "end-to-end" measurement (headers to capture, timestamps to look at).

-Alex

Subject: Re: Performance SLO (p95/p99) qualification - Hosted API vs current provider - post-call recap

Hi Alex / Samir — 

Thanks for the trace — very useful. Quick answers and proposed plan from an infra/measurement perspective: 

Measurement definitions (what Redwood reports):
- "End-to-end" = time at API ingress (when request accepted by Redwood public endpoint) -> time when last token is emitted by Redwood runtime. This includes our network and runtime time, and any gateway processing. It does not include the customer client network time to our edge.
- For streaming: we report both "time-to-first-token" and a distribution of inter-token latencies for the first N tokens; we surface p50/p95/p99 for both metrics.

Cold-starts / warm pools:
- Hosted: we maintain a small warm pool per model variant for common workloads; cold-starts are possible for very long-context or rarely-used model variants. For stricter SLOs, Dedicated capacity gives stronger isolation and faster scale-up.

How we'll validate for Finlytics:
1) We mirror your trace pattern and run two types of tests: steady-state RPS (to validate throughput + tail latency) and mixed interactive streams (to validate TTFB under concurrency).
2) We'll run both us-west and eu-west since you requested region parity.
3) We will run an initial smoke run to calibrate batch sizes and KV cache behavior, then run 3 full-load runs at peak concurrency windows you expect.

Recommended config for your targets:
- Reserved capacity with 1.5x buffer over expected peak QPS for the evaluation week.
- Streaming enabled with smaller micro-batches (we'll tune during smoke run).
- If p99 under sustained peak is critical, recommend Dedicated capacity for production.

Attachments: the redwood-p95-p99-sla-table.xlsx I shared earlier defines the measurement points and what we exclude/include. I also attached a sample run (perf-sample-results.pdf) with similar concurrency.

Jonas — can we take point on running the tech-run and share a short test checklist + temporary eval credentials?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
